title: Game Developer
description: End-to-end game development: 2D/3D game math, game loops, physics & collisions, engine architecture, input juice, state machines, animations, audio, AI (A* and behavior trees), shaders, optimization, and game publishing.

phases.title: Game Math & Architecture Foundations
phases.focus: Vector Math, Game Loop Timesteps, Collision Detection & Engine Component Hierarchies

phases.title: Gameplay Systems & AI Core
phases.focus: Player Input Juice, State Machines, Blend Trees, Adaptive Audio & Behavior Tree AI

phases.title: Visuals, Shaders & Optimization
phases.focus: HLSL Shaders, GPU Particles, Level Design, Save Systems & Profiling Optimization

phases.title: Multiplayer & Commercial Capstone
phases.focus: Client-Side Prediction, Responsive Game UI, and Polished Vertical Slice Release

nodes.title: Game Math & Physics Foundations
nodes.subtitle: 2D/3D vectors, dot product, cross product, vector normalization, radians, coordinate spaces
learning_objectives: Calculate angles, directions, and distances between game objects using vector math
Apply dot products to determine field-of-view visibility and directional facing
feynman_prompts: Explain what the dot product of two normalized vectors reveals about their direction.
key_misconceptions: Mixing up local coordinate space with global world coordinate space

nodes.title: Game Loop Architecture & Delta Time
nodes.subtitle: FixedUpdate vs Update, variable vs fixed timestep, delta time, frame rate independence, vsync
learning_objectives: Implement frame-rate-independent character movement using delta time
Distinguish physics simulation ticks (fixed timestep) from visual rendering ticks
feynman_prompts: Why does moving an object by speed without multiplying by delta time break at different FPS?
key_misconceptions: Placing physics calculations inside the variable-rate render loop

nodes.title: Collision Detection & 2D Physics
nodes.subtitle: AABB (Axis-Aligned Bounding Box), Circle-Circle collision, SAT (Separating Axis Theorem), raycasting
learning_objectives: Implement AABB and circle collision detection algorithms from scratch
Perform raycasts to detect ground surfaces, obstacles, and line-of-sight in 2D/3D
feynman_prompts: Explain how Separating Axis Theorem (SAT) detects collisions between rotated convex polygons.
key_misconceptions: Assuming bounding boxes must always be oriented along the screen axes (ignoring rotation)

nodes.title: Game Engine Fundamentals: Unity / Godot / Unreal
nodes.subtitle: Game objects, actors, components, transforms, prefabs/scenes, script lifecycles (Awake, Start, Update)
learning_objectives: Structure game entities using component composition over rigid object-oriented inheritance
Instantiate and configure dynamic game object prefabs at runtime
feynman_prompts: Why is composition (adding components) superior to deep class inheritance in game architecture?
key_misconceptions: Creating monolithic God-classes that handle input, audio, rendering, and physics all in one script

nodes.title: Input Systems & Player Controller 'Juice'
nodes.subtitle: New Input System, action maps, buffering, coyote time, jump apex gravity tuning, screenshake
learning_objectives: Tune player controller physics with jump buffering, coyote time, and variable jump height
Add 'game juice' (screen shake, hit-stop freeze frames, particle bursts) to heighten responsiveness
feynman_prompts: What is coyote time and why does it make platformer jump controls feel fair to players?
key_misconceptions: Relying strictly on realistic raw physics equations without tuning for game feel and responsiveness

nodes.title: Game State Management & Finite State Machines (FSM)
nodes.subtitle: FSM architecture, character state machines (Idle, Run, Jump, Attack, Hurt), hierarchical state machines
learning_objectives: Build clean finite state machines for complex player character and enemy state management
Prevent illegal animation and logic transitions (e.g. attacking while dodging) using explicit FSM states
feynman_prompts: Why does using boolean flags (`isJumping`, `isAttacking`, `isDead`) quickly lead to spaghetti code?
key_misconceptions: Allowing multiple conflicting character states to be active simultaneously

nodes.title: Animation Systems & Blend Trees
nodes.subtitle: Skeletal animation, state machine transitions, blend trees, inverse kinematics (IK), root motion
learning_objectives: Configure 1D and 2D animation blend trees for smooth locomotion transitions (walk to sprint)
Apply two-bone Inverse Kinematics (IK) to anchor character feet to uneven ground geometry
feynman_prompts: Explain how animation blend trees interpolate between multiple directional movement clips.
key_misconceptions: Hard-snapping between animations without transition cross-fading

nodes.title: Game Audio Architecture & Adaptive Sound
nodes.subtitle: Audio listeners, 3D spatial sound, audio mixers, ducking, adaptive music layering, sound cues
learning_objectives: Implement 3D spatial attenuation and sound occlusion based on room geometry
Design dynamic music systems that transition stems based on combat intensity
feynman_prompts: How does dynamic audio ducking prevent sound clipping during intense explosion sequences?
key_misconceptions: Playing repetitive sound effects at constant volume and pitch without subtle random variations

nodes.title: Game AI & Pathfinding: A* and NavMesh
nodes.subtitle: A* algorithm, heuristic functions, navigation meshes (NavMesh), agent steering, avoidance
learning_objectives: Implement the A* pathfinding algorithm on grid and node graph representations
Bake dynamic NavMeshes and configure AI agent obstacle avoidance in 3D worlds
feynman_prompts: Explain how the heuristic function in A* guides the search towards the target faster than Dijkstra.
key_misconceptions: Recalculating complete pathfinding routes every single frame for dozens of enemies

nodes.title: Advanced AI: Behavior Trees & Utility AI
nodes.subtitle: Behavior trees (Sequencer, Selector, Decorators, Blackboard), utility AI, sensory perception
learning_objectives: Design modular behavior trees with composite nodes and decorators for intelligent enemy AI
Implement sensory perception systems (hearing footsteps, field-of-view cone detection)
feynman_prompts: Why are behavior trees more scalable for complex game AI than massive finite state machines?
key_misconceptions: Hardcoding AI logic directly into game update loops instead of blackboard data

nodes.title: Graphics Pipeline, Shaders & Materials
nodes.subtitle: Vertex & fragment shaders, HLSL/Shader Graph, PBR materials, normal maps, lighting models
learning_objectives: Write custom fragment shaders for rim lighting, dissolve effects, and water surfaces
Configure Physically Based Rendering (PBR) materials with albedo, metallic, roughness, and normal maps
feynman_prompts: Explain the difference in responsibility between vertex shaders and fragment/pixel shaders.
key_misconceptions: Executing expensive mathematical calculations in fragment shaders that could be computed once in vertex shaders

nodes.title: VFX & Particle Systems (VFX Graph / Niagara)
nodes.subtitle: GPU particles, emitter modules, forces, turbulence, sprite sheets, particle collision
learning_objectives: Author high-performance GPU particle simulations for spells, fire, and weather effects
Trigger context-aware impact particle effects matched to surface physical materials
feynman_prompts: Why do GPU particle systems handle millions of particles while CPU systems choke on thousands?
key_misconceptions: Spawning separate particle game objects dynamically instead of recycling via object pooling

nodes.title: Level Design, Whiteboxing & Environmental Storytelling
nodes.subtitle: Grayboxing/whiteboxing, sightlines, breadcrumbing, choke points, pacing, lighting cues
learning_objectives: Block out playable 3D levels using primitive geometry to test pacing and player metrics
Guide player navigation naturally using architectural lighting, leading lines, and color contrast
feynman_prompts: Why should gameplay levels be thoroughly playtested in graybox before any 3D art is created?
key_misconceptions: Decorating an unplayable, confusing level with final high-poly art assets

nodes.title: Save Systems, Persistence & Serialization
nodes.subtitle: JSON/binary serialization, save versioning, encryption, cloud saves, state persistence
learning_objectives: Architect robust save/load systems capable of serializing dynamic world and inventory state
Implement save file versioning and migration to prevent breaking user saves on game patches
feynman_prompts: How do you prevent players from modifying local plaintext save files to cheat progression?
key_misconceptions: Attempting to serialize raw game engine objects directly instead of clean data transfer DTOs

nodes.title: Game Optimization, Profiling & Memory Management
nodes.subtitle: CPU/GPU profiler, draw calls, dynamic/static batching, LODs, occlusion culling, garbage collection
learning_objectives: Profile frame spikes, identify GC memory allocations, and eliminate runtime heap churn
Reduce draw calls using GPU instancing, texture atlases, and occlusion culling
feynman_prompts: Explain how garbage collection pauses cause noticeable micro-stutters during high-speed gameplay.
key_misconceptions: Instantiating and destroying hundreds of projectiles per minute instead of using an Object Pool

nodes.title: Multiplayer Fundamentals & Client-Side Prediction
nodes.subtitle: Client-server architecture, client-side prediction, server reconciliation, entity interpolation
learning_objectives: Implement client-side movement prediction with server authoritative snapshot reconciliation
Interpolate remote player positions smoothly across variable network latency
feynman_prompts: Why must the server remain authoritative over player position and health in multiplayer games?
key_misconceptions: Trusting the client to report when it takes damage or where it moves

nodes.title: Game UI, Accessibility & Localization
nodes.subtitle: Canvas scalability, screen-safe areas, gamepad navigation, input glyph rebinding, localization tables
learning_objectives: Design responsive game HUDs and menus that scale across ultrawide and handheld resolutions
Implement full gamepad navigation, UI audio feedback, and dynamic subtitle font scaling
feynman_prompts: Why must UI layouts be designed with flexible text bounding boxes for international localization?
key_misconceptions: Hardcoding string text directly inside UI scripts and buttons

nodes.title: Full Game Polish & Release Capstone
nodes.subtitle: Vertical slice development, platform SDKs (Steamworks/Console), bug hunting, build pipelines
learning_objectives: Build, profile, and package a polished commercial vertical slice game demo
Integrate platform SDKs (achievements, cloud saves, leaderboards) and automated build pipelines
feynman_prompts: What differentiates a completed, polished game from an unfinished prototype?
key_misconceptions: Spending years adding feature after feature to a game without ever locking scope and polishing
